subject: Week 41: narrate the whole day — first words run on input, not drills
bodyText:
This week
Days 285 through 291: self-feeding is more refined, most soft family foods are on the table, and he can drink from a cup with help. Cruising is fluent for many and first steps arrive for some — the CDC walks-alone checkpoint stays at 15 months. Expressive vocabulary right now can be zero to five words and both ends sit inside the range; the growth is on the receptive side, and it responds to input volume and back-and-forth rather than to drilling.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Refusal of foods he ate happily last month — preference churn is standard here; keep offering the rejected food without pressure or substitution.
- [low concern] No words at all. About 25% of 12-month-olds are not yet using words, and the CDC checkpoint for words beyond mama and dada is 15 months.
- [monitor] Rich babble but no gestures — no waving, no showing, no arms up. The gesture channel carries more weight than word count at this age.
- [call within 24h] Night waking with crying plus ear-pulling after a cold, or fever above 102F rectal with ear drainage — otitis media peaks between 6 and 24 months.
- [call now] Fever ≥102F rectal with lethargy, or respiratory distress with retractions or grunting; blue lips or unresponsiveness is 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Narrate the two hours you are with him most — bath, dinner prep, the walk — and name what he is already looking at instead of redirecting him to what you wanted to name. Words that land on the object he chose get mapped faster, and pausing after every sound he makes turns narration into the conversational turns that predicted language-network activation years later. Romeo et al. 2018 (PubMed): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Teach the way down: from standing at the couch, guide his hands toward the floor and let his knees fold. Getting down is a separate skill from getting up, and it is the one that prevents the stiff backward fall. AAP: Movement 8 to 12 Months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-8-to-12-Months.aspx
- Move him onto the family menu with three rules: soft enough to squash between thumb and finger, cut smaller than a marble, and nothing round left whole — grapes quartered lengthwise, no whole nuts, no popcorn, no hot-dog coins. AAP: Starting Solid Foods: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/feeding-nutrition/Pages/Starting-Solid-Foods.aspx
- Buy outdoor shoes only once he is actually walking outside: a sole you can twist, a thumb-width of room at the toe, no ankle support. Indoors stays barefoot, which is still the better surface for balance learning.

Upcoming
- Day 280 (Feb 15, 2027) has passed and the 9-month visit window is closed — if the visit never happened, book it now as a late well visit rather than waiting for the 12-month slot.
- Day 292-298 (Feb 27–Mar 5, 2027): 11-month landmark — open the 12-month visit notes file then: word list, sleep pattern, eating range, motor checkpoints.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Plays peekaboo (initiates by covering and uncovering face)
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Active game initiation, not just smiling when you hide. Demonstrates object permanence in action.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/plays-peekaboo/complete

- Plays games like pat-a-cake
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Imitative gesture game. Joint attention + motor imitation.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/plays-pat-a-cake/complete

- Waves bye-bye
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Intentional gesture with social meaning.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/waves-bye/complete

- Calls a parent 'mama' or 'dada' or another name
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Specifically referring to a person, not generalized babble. First true word for many babies.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/calls-parent-by-name/complete

- Understands 'no' (pauses or stops when you say it)
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Receptive language. Compliance is a much later milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/understands-no/complete
